text:
sofia: quick note — recent dedicated carveouts still hit PCIe congestion. root-complex sharing seems the culprit. proposing a small rollout to detect and tag PCIe root ids and prefer spread across roots for carveouts.

rahul: good catch. want an inventory tag `pcie_root_id` and a `--check-root` preflight on carveout CLI.

emily: will write a lightweight discovery script (ssh + lspci) and push tags to inventory. canary on rack21.

javier: keep TTL short (7d) and cache in scheduler (10s). avoids cardinality blowup. finance: add cost-tag when we migrate.

infra-bot: DISCOVERY-SCHEDULED: discovery-canary for rack21 at 2026-03-25T02:00:00Z. Ticket INV-8902.

sofia: rollout plan: canary discovery -> enable `spread_root_complex` for carveouts in staging -> monitor pcie_stalls, placement_latency for 12h -> stage to more racks. rollback flips flag + rebalancer.

emily: sample commands:
```
ansible-playbook playbooks/discover_pcie_root.yml --limit=rack21-host[01:04]
inventoryctl tag push --source=discover-canary --ttl=7d --hosts=rack21-host[01..04]
schedulerctl feature-flag set spread_root_complex=true --scope=carveouts
fleetctl carveout create --tenant=t-vision --cards=1 --region=us-west2 --check-root
```

rahul: i'll add scheduler unit tests for spread behavior. sofia will own canary and post results here.
